facts.fact: Ghana Police Service said at a 30 March 2026 briefing that creating, sharing or promoting deepfake content targeting public figures is a criminal offence under Ghana's laws, though no specific law was cited.

Police arrested two suspects on 28 March 2026 over deepfake videos impersonating President Mahama and the First Lady used to solicit investment funds, after forensic analysis by the CID Cybercrime Enforcement Team.

GHA.note: Document states nothing on government use of AI.
Document states nothing on AI in a sector's public system.
Document states nothing on AI built or hosted in Ghana.

facts.fact: Graphic Online states that provisions under the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038) criminalise publishing and sharing false or misleading digital content and unauthorised access to data.

GHA.note: Arrests were reported but the police cited no specific law, so no use of the Act is recorded.
Arrests were for deepfake investment fraud and a threat against a judge, not for speech about government.
Document states nothing on station records.
